To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of different types of anesthesia in carotid endarterectomy has different effects on cognitive function of patients.

the use of sevofluorine for general anesthesia during carotid artery surgery leads to a more pronounced cognitive deficit in comparison to propofol, and that the use of regional anesthesia in the combination of reduced general anesthesia causes a less pronounced cognitive deficit in patients with symptomic or asymptomatic steno-sis.
the use of regional anesthesia in the combination of reduced general anesthesia caused less pronounced cognitive deficits compared with inhalation anesthesia with sevolfuorane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods of anesthesia for carotid surgery and correction of postoperative cognitive dysfunction.
the development of a new concept of the anesthesia management in patients with carotid steno-occlusive disease.
the development of a new approach to the correction of the cognitive impairment in the postoperative period after surgical interventions in carotid arteries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of the type of anesthesia in carotid endarterectomy is a matter of debate and should be made by the anesthesiologist and neurosurgeon in the context of a multidisciplinary approach.

the use of regional anesthesia in combination with reduced general inhalation anesthesia in patients with carotid stenting and carotid endarterectomy is the most effective and safest method of anesthesia.
the use of sevofluorine anesthesia is associated with a higher incidence of postoperative cognitive dysfunction in patients after carotid endarterectomy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of different types of anesthesia during carotid surgery is an important risk factor for cognitive impairment, which is more expressed in patients with symptomic carotid stenosys.
regional anesthesia in the combination of reduced general anesthesia caused a less pronounced cognitive impairment after reconstructive surgeries of the carotid arteries.
regional anesthesia in combination with reduced general one is preferable for patients undergoing the surgical intervention on carotid arteries, especially in case of symptomatic stenosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
regional anesthesia in the combination of reduced general anesthesia is the most optimal for the patients undergoing reconstructive surgeries of carotid artery stenoses.
the use of regional anesthesia with reduced general anesthesia and total intravenous anesthesia is preferable for the reconstructive surgeries for atheroscleroting stenosis of carotid artery.
the type of anesthesia used in the surgical treatment of carotid artery stenosis can significantly affect the dynamics of cognitive functions.
